messages.content: Let's pick up a packet inspector.
Picking up a packet inspector.
Progress?
src/codec/mod.rs ended up with most of the changes.
Progress?

Most of the work happened inside fuzz/fuzz_targets/decode.rs. Good news: zero-copy deserialisation of the record header made it in before the freeze. benches/parse.rs ended up with most of the changes.
Issues?
I'll summarise at the end. The alerts this morning came from unbounded memory growth in the buffer pool.
Serde with a custom binary format sounds like the better deal to me.
Documenting the public API surface is waiting for someone to pick it up. The streaming parser over a bounded buffer? Taken care of. Okay, doing it.
Any errors?
Fuzzing the input decoder with cargo-fuzz went smoothly in the end. An arena allocator for the parse nodes is what we'll ship with. Failed jobs are retried twice.
Keep going.
Rust 2021 edition with MSRV 1.75 beat the alternatives on every axis we care about. Property tests over the encoder round trip went smoothly in the end.
What's done?
A workspace layout with three crates beat the alternatives on every axis we care about. Everyone was happy with clap for argument parsing.
What about a packet inspector?
Everyone was happy with tokio over async-std for the runtime.
Plan for a packet inspector?
We can stop worrying about error types unified behind thiserror now. A lock-free ring buffer for the writer? Taken care of. Let me know if anything looks off.
